Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Painful, itchy, cracked skin on palms and fingers; symptoms present 3–4 months, recently worsened to the point patient missed 3 days of work.
- Aggravating factors: Cleaning products used at work; patient frequently forgets to wear gloves.
- Associated features: Occasional bleeding after scratching; generalized mild skin dryness on legs; no fever, GI, GU, or systemic symptoms.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medications:
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • OTC emollient (E45) – ineffective.  
  • OTC antihistamine – ineffective; name/dose not documented.
- Social history:
  • Occupation: Hotel housekeeper.  
  • Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
  • Alcohol: “A couple of pints” once per week.  
  • Glove use at work inconsistent.
- Family history: Diabetes mellitus; no known dermatologic conditions.
- Allergies: Denies drug or environmental allergies.

Objective:
- No in-person examination performed (telehealth visit).
- No vitals available.
- No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Hand dermatitis (likely irritant/contact dermatitis):
   - Assessment: Chronic irritant/contact dermatitis of palms/fingers, likely due to occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals.
   - Investigations planned: None at this time.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Topical mid-potency corticosteroid cream (prescription sent electronically to patient’s pharmacy).  
     • High-lipid emollient moisturizer; apply generously 3–4 times daily.  
     • Strict trigger avoidance: wear protective gloves for all cleaning tasks.  
   - Follow-up: Reassess in 10–14 days; sooner if spread or worsening.
